$why: What the repro-writer is told when its previous attempt failed, in the two ways it can: the test did not COMPILE, or it compiled and its assertions failed against a fix that is already committed. The second is the harder message to get right -- a failing assertion there means the TEST is wrong, not the code, and a writer told otherwise will 'fix' working code.

The compiler errors arrived through a grep | head -8 pipeline inside the prompt -- a truncation of the very errors the writer is told to eliminate, so error nine onward were invisible and the rewrite could never be complete. The caller supplies them.
And the failure JSON arrived head -c 1200 -- cut at a byte offset, mid-structure, so what the writer was shown of its own failure was not valid JSON at all.

A third way the previous attempt can fail, added 2026-09-11: the test compiled and passed and the CLIENT REPOSITORY refused to commit it. Live on AMSD-1919, lint-staged rejected one `export` (jest/no-export); the test stayed uncommitted, the repro gate blocked, and the whole story was re-implemented. The hook output is the rejection reason, quoted verbatim — the engine knows no hook rule.
description: Feedback to the repro-writer when its previous test failed to compile or failed its assertions.

bodies.typecheck:
## COMPILER ERRORS FROM YOUR PREVIOUS ATTEMPT — FIX THESE
Your last test ran but did NOT compile. tsc reported, for this exact file:
```
__COMPILER_ERRORS__
```
Rewrite the file so these are gone. Mock objects must satisfy the full type.
bodies.assertions:
## YOUR TEST FAILED AGAINST THE FIX THAT IS ALREADY COMMITTED
The change for this story is ALREADY in the working tree. Your test ran but __FAILED__ of __TOTAL__ assertion(s) FAILED, which means your test contradicts the implemented change.
Read the diff above again and assert the behaviour it ACTUALLY produces.
```
__FAILURE_JSON__
```
bodies.commitRejected:
## THE REPOSITORY REJECTED YOUR PREVIOUS TEST AT COMMIT — FIX WHAT IT NAMES
Your last test compiled and passed, and the repository refused to commit it. Its own commit hook reported:
```
__HOOK_OUTPUT__
```
The file is still in place. Change ONLY what the hook names, keep every assertion, and write it again to the same path.
